status: Literature-informed contact/seal concerns; not service-life prediction

sources.evidence: 5413 polyimide film plus silicone adhesive, solder masking, upper temperature260C; no continuously molten solder seal qualification supplied.
sources.inference: Do not substitute bare film heat resistance for adhesive joint qualification.

sources.evidence: Copper-core soldering tips use iron plating for corrosion resistance; lead-free and elevated temperatures shorten life.

sources.title: Pronounced electromigration of Cu in molten Sn-based solders, Huang et al., J Mater Res23(1),2008
sources.evidence: Molten Sn3.5Ag at255C, continuous6300A/cm2; pronounced cathode copper dissolution and anode intermetallic accumulation compared with no-current controls.
sources.limit: Different alloy/current/geometry; not a lifetime scaling law for our pulsed nozzle.

sources.evidence: Ordinary galvanic-corrosion description requires coupled dissimilar materials and corrosive electrolyte.
sources.inference: Molten solder current is metallic conduction; dissolution and electromigration are the more directly supported contact mechanisms here.

next_measurements: No-current soak and matched-temperature pulse coupons for both solders, copper and316SS.
Inspect bore growth, electrode recession, wetting, deposits and leakage over time; compare pulse polarity.
Four-wire joint resistance and actual peak contact temperature; RMS alone does not bound a contact hot spot.
design_preference: Replaceable mechanically clamped strip worth exploring. Continuous copper may bypass liquid current; isolate conductivity from geometry in native solves. Adhesive-free gasket remains unqualified, not specified as a proven hot seal.
